subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: For macOS app-backed nodes, should OpenClaw preserve advertised `system.which`/`system.run` and make remote skill-bin probing readiness-aware, or should it skip/disable probes for co-located app nodes?
rationale: Current main has partial mitigations but no live proof that startup/reconnect probe timing is fixed; choosing skip, defer, retry, and backoff semantics affects node exec compatibility and user-visible skill availability.

options.title: Defer and back off readiness-aware probes
options.body: Preserve the macOS app node command surface, delay the initial probe until the node is ready, add bounded retry/backoff, and require live proof for co-located and remote macOS app nodes.

options.title: Skip only co-located app probes
options.body: Avoid the local gateway/app warning case, but leave the reported remote macOS app timing issue as a separate unresolved path.

options.title: Add a global disable flag
options.body: This would suppress symptoms for operators but adds config surface and leaves the core node-readiness behavior unresolved.

recommendation.title: Defer and back off readiness-aware probes
recommendation.body: Preserve the macOS app node command surface, delay the initial probe until the node is ready, add bounded retry/backoff, and require live proof for co-located and remote macOS app nodes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad ownership of gateway node policy, docs, and node protocol maintenance decisions around this surface.
